summary: Console alert tracehook drift after multi-tenant rollout causing stale deep-links
description: Issue summary: After a staged multi-tenant rollout of the console routing changes (rollout v2026-03/mt-routing), alert deep-links generated by scheduled heatmap and panel alerts open dashboards with stale time anchors or missing tracehook parameters. Impact: DataWeave reports multiple alerts linking to dashboards where tracehook context is stripped or points to a default/old time window, preventing engineers from jumping to the relevant trace. This affects their incident triage workflow and increases time-to-resolution for customer-facing incidents. Environment: prod/us-east; console requests and alert evaluation pipelines. Timeline: problem first observed after canary (tenant slice 4) moved to 50% traffic on 2026-03-10 21:00 UTC. Expected: alert deep-links should preserve the original tracehook token and time bounds used at evaluation time. Observed: links either resolve to an expired token (redirect to overview) or to a stale anchor (time window shifted by hours).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In DataWeave org create a scheduled heatmap alert with tracehook=true and 15m evaluation window
2) Wait for an alert firing event and copy the deep-link from the alert notification
3) Open deep-link in a private browser session (incognito) or with cleared cookies
4) Observe console opens but timeframe and tracehook context are not preserved (either redirected to default overview or an older time range)
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): confirmed multiple customers in tenant-slice 4 and 5 reported link drift after rollout toggle
SRE reproduced in staging by toggling routing flags; observed tracehook token lookup returned 404 for some tenant-scoped mapping keys
Hypothesis A: retention compaction removed cached mapping used by alert linker when the mapping TTL wasn't refreshed during the rollout
Hypothesis B: session-affinity change caused alert evaluation to be executed by a worker that didn't have the new linker migration applied, producing older-format tokens
Heap of evidence: timing of compaction sweep (gc-compact-2026-03-10T20:58Z) coincides with first reports; consumer-lag on linker-index topic shows retry spikes
Test performed: reproduced by forcing a compaction and triggering an alert - consistent reproduction observed when compaction and evaluation windows overlap
Risk assessment: affects deep-links only; console rendering and raw trace ingestion unaffected. However it materially increases incident MTTR for enterprise customers relying on tracehooks.

resolution: Workaround: Rolled back tenant routing toggle for affected slices and queued a backfill to repopulate missing tracehook mappings. Fix: Deployed linker TTL renewal patch (v2026-03.13) which ensures tokens are renewed on write during migration and adds idempotent key creation to avoid compaction races. Backfill completed for 03/10-03/12 alert events. Follow-ups: add integration test simulating compaction+evaluation, add alert for linker-index topic lag > 30s, and update runbook to avoid scheduling compaction sweep during active rollouts.
